title: On-call & Incident Response Playbook
author: Asha Patel
content:
Summary:

This playbook documents Redwood Inference's on-call and incident response process. It covers severity definitions and SLAs, roles and responsibilities, runbook patterns for common systems (inference-api, router, cache, kv-store), the postmortem template, on-call rotations and handoffs, game day guidance, and customer-facing status page / communications templates. Use this as the canonical reference for operating incidents and for preparing runbook-run exercises.

Scope:
- Applies to production incidents affecting availability, correctness, data safety, or security for any Redwood-hosted or Dedicated/Private customer surface.
- Non-production issues (staging/dev) should follow team-specific runbooks unless the issue escalates to cross-team impact.

1) Incident severity definitions and target SLAs

Severity levels (summary table):
- SEV0: Total outage for >10% customers or system-wide data loss. Response: immediate. Acknowledge within 5 minutes. Mitigate within 30 minutes or follow executive comms.
- SEV1: Major degradation (API errors >10% or latency >5x baseline for >5 minutes). Acknowledge within 10 minutes. Mitigate within 60 minutes.
- SEV2: Partial degradation (reduced throughput, elevated errors for a subset of customers). Acknowledge within 30 minutes. Mitigate within 4 hours.
- SEV3: Minor operational issues or single-customer incidents without impacting SLAs. Acknowledge within 8 business hours. Mitigation timelines by owner team.

SLOs & escalation thresholds (quick reference):
- Acknowledgement SLA = time-to-first-response in PagerDuty.
- Mitigation SLA = time-to-reduce user-visible impact by 80%.
- If SLA missed, auto-escalate to on-call manager and platform lead.

2) Roles and responsibilities

- Incident Commander (IC): Owns the incident lifecycle, decisions, and timeline. Declares severity, coordinates mitigation, and authorizes customer comms.
- Scribe: Records timeline, actions taken, and artifacts (logs, traces, screenshots).
- Communications Lead: Manages internal and external messaging (Slack bridge, status page, customer emails).
- Subject Matter Experts (SMEs): Provide technical remediation steps for affected services.
- On-call Engineer: First responder alerted by PagerDuty. Performs initial triage and hands off to IC if incident escalates.
- Incident Manager / Postmortem Lead: Drives the post-incident review and action items.

Channels and tooling:
- Pager: PagerDuty (primary) with escalation policy per rotation.
- Chat: Slack channels #oncall, #incidents, and service-specific channels (e.g., #inference-api). Use Slack incident bridge when SEV0/1 declared.
- Incident tracking: Jira project INF-INC for active incident tickets and postmortems.
- Status page: status.redwood.ai (internal & customer-facing components).

3) Incident lifecycle (step-by-step)

1. Detection & Alerting:
   - PagerDuty triggers. Monitoring signals include: 5xx ratio, p50/p95/p99 latency, queue depth, error budgets, and user reports.
   - Provide short description and PagerDuty evidence (logs link, runbook link).
2. Triage (first 10 minutes):
   - On-call Engineer runs initial checks (see runbook checklist below).
   - Confirm scope (affected services/customers/regions).
   - Determine preliminary severity and notify IC if escalation indicated.
3. Mitigation (ongoing):
   - IC coordinates mitigation path: rollback, scale, config change, traffic remap, or fallback to alternative model/instance.
   - Document every change (who, what, why, and rollback plan).
4. Recovery & Verification:
   - Validate customer impact is reduced to acceptable level. Run synthetic checks and confirm with monitoring dashboards.
5. Communication:
   - Internal: Slack incident channel, incident summary every 30–60 minutes for SEV0/1.
   - External: Update status page and notify customers per comms template.
6. Post-incident:
   - IC declares incident closed when verified; create Jira incident ticket if not auto-created.
   - Conduct postmortem within 5 business days for SEV0/1 and within 10 business days for SEV2.

4) Runbook pattern & example checks

Runbook pattern (for each service):
- Purpose: short description of what the service does and primary impact modes.
- Symptoms: monitoring signals that map to user-visible problems.
- Initial triage commands and queries.
- Quick mitigations (safe, reversible steps).
- Escalation path and SMEs.
- Post-incident actions to add to the runbook.

Example: inference-api quick triage checklist:
- Check external symptoms:
  - curl -sS -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} %{time_total}\n" "https://inference-api.prod.redwood.ai/healthz"
  - kubectl -n inference get pods -l app=inference-api
- Check error rates:
  - Grafana dashboard: Inference -> Errors (last 15m).
  - Loki query (example): {app=\"inference-api\"} | json | status >= 500 | count_over_time(1m)
  - (CLI sample) rlogs --service inference-api --since 15m --level error | head -n 200
- Safe mitigations:
  - If pods are crashlooping: kubectl describe pod <pod> ; kubectl logs <pod> --previous
  - If CPU saturation: scale deployment: kubectl -n inference scale deploy inference-api --replicas=<n+2>
  - If configuration issue (recent deploy): rollback: kubectl -n inference rollout undo deploy/inference-api --to-revision=<rev>
- Escalation: oncall -> IC -> platform-runtime -> infra/networking depending on root cause.

5) Postmortem template (required fields)

- Title (short, descriptive)
- Severity (SEV0/1/2/3)
- Impact summary (customers, regions, features)
- Timeline (UTC): bullet-list of timestamps, actions, and outcomes.
- Root cause analysis: what failed and why (include logs/traces).
- Contributing factors: human, process, tooling, or environmental.
- Mitigations taken during incident and permanent fixes planned.
- Action items (owner, due date, validation criteria).
- Learnings and follow-up game day if appropriate.

Postmortem expectations: Avoid blame; be factual and cite evidence. Each action item must have an owner and a verification plan. Postmortems for SEV0/1 require a follow-up check-in 30 days after the fix is deployed.

6) On-call rotations and handoffs

Rotation cadence and structure:
- Primary on-call: 1 week rotation. Secondary (backup) on-call: same cadence.
- On-call manager: monthly rotation.
- Typical handoff: 15-minute overlap between shifts for critical services. Handoff checklist:
  1) Review open incidents and current status.
  2) Verify dashboards and on-call runbook links.
  3) Confirm access keys and tooling (PagerDuty, Slack, kubectl, rlogs).
  4) Note planned maintenance windows or deploys.

Escalation policy (summary):
- If primary does not acknowledge within SLA window, PagerDuty escalates to secondary.
- If secondary fails to respond or incident reaches time-to-mitigate threshold, escalate to on-call manager and platform lead.

7) Game days and runbook validation

Purpose: Validate runbooks, tooling, and coordination under realistic conditions.
- Frequency: Quarterly platform-wide game days and monthly team-level exercises.
- Realistic scenarios: deploy failure, network partition, degraded GPU capacity, KV-store corruption, model quality regression.
- Game day checklist:
  - Pre-game: define scope, simulate traffic, create monitoring baselines.
  - During: runbook-driven triage, enforce timed updates, record timeline.
  - Post-game: action items, update runbooks, and publish a game day report.

8) Status page & customer communications templates

Status page update template (short):
- Title: [INVESTIGATION] Inference API elevated error rate
- Update: We are investigating an increase in 5xx errors for the Inference API impacting API calls for a subset of customers. Engineers are actively investigating.
- Time: 2026-02-12T14:20:00Z
- Next update: within 30 minutes or when status changes

Customer-facing email template (use for SEV0/1 after IC sign-off):
- Subject: Incident update: Redwood Inference degradation on <service> (yyyy-mm-dd)
- Body: Hello <CustomerName>,
  We want to inform you of an incident affecting <service>. Summary: [brief impact]. Current status: [investigating / mitigated / resolved]. Actions taken: [short list]. Customer impact: [who/what]. Expected next update: [time]. If you have questions, contact <support link> or reply to this email.
  Thank you for your patience,
  Redwood Inference Operations

Internal Slack update cadence (for SEV0/1):
- T+0: Initial alert + short summary + IC assigned
- T+15: Triage summary (scope, hypothesis, immediate mitigation)
- Every 30–60m: Status update until mitigation achieved
- On recovery: short summary + postmortem ETA

9) Runbook hygiene and ownership

- Every runbook must have an owner and last-reviewed date. Review cadence: every 6 months or after a related incident.
- After each incident, update the runbook with the new steps and add any automation that reduces time-to-mitigate.
- Label runbooks with service tags and add links to the Jira incident and postmortem.

10) Appendix: Useful commands and monitoring queries

- K8s quick-checks:
  - kubectl -n inference get pods -o wide
  - kubectl -n inference describe pod <pod>
  - kubectl -n inference logs <pod> --since=10m
- Healthcheck curl:
  - curl -fS https://inference-api.prod.redwood.ai/healthz || true
- Loki sample queries:
  - {app=\"inference-api\", level=\"error\"} |= \"timeout\" | count_over_time(5m)
- Grafana alerts to check: Inference > RequestErrorRate, GPU Utilization, KV-store latency

Ownership and contact
- PagerDuty escalation: infra-pager (primary), platform-pager (secondary).
- Slack: #oncall for alerts, #incidents for cross-team coordination.
- Runbooks repo: internal wiki links under /confluence/eng-sre/runbooks (maintained by eng-sre).

Document maintenance
- Owner: Asha Patel (engineering)
- Review cycle: 6 months or after any SEV0/1 incident.

End of document.
